$comment: Every non-shell screen in supplement.product.aging.json. Shell screens SH1–SH6 are deliberately absent: they are identical in every programme and are not this file's to write. The person throughout is Ruth, 74, in a bungalow with a back step that has caught her twice; her daughter Carol is twenty minutes away and Dev is her coach. Every string is unreviewed.

S01.headline: Staying on your own two feet.
S01.sub: Steady is a minute a day, in your own words, about the things that keep you doing what you already do. It is not a monitor, and it is not somebody keeping an eye on you.

blocks.title: Nobody is watching
blocks.body: No location, no listening, no camera, no alarm that goes off in someone else's kitchen. A family member sees the small thing you agreed to send them, on the day you send it.

blocks.title: You decide, every time
blocks.body: Someone can help you without taking anything over. They can't change your plan, answer for you, or overrule you. That isn't a setting you have to find — there's no button for it on their side at all.

blocks.title: Built to be read
blocks.body: Large text throughout, big buttons, strong contrast. If your phone's text is set large, this follows it, and you can go larger still.

S01.footer: Education and self-management support. Not a diagnosis or treatment.

S02.title: What it does
S02.headline: Four moments this is built for.
S02.sub: Not four features. Four things that actually come up.

blocks.title: When you're not sure whether this year is different
blocks.body: A week of noticing first. How steady you felt, and how long you were on your feet. You say it, we write it down, and nothing is graded.

blocks.title: When the back step catches you
blocks.body: A wobble goes in the same day, in one tap. It isn't a failure and it isn't an alarm. It's the thing that tells you which step to sort out.

blocks.title: When Carol rings to ask how you are
blocks.body: She's already seen the line you sent on Sunday, so the call can be about something else for once.

blocks.title: When something is actually wrong
blocks.body: A route to a qualified person, in the same place on every screen, never reordered and never hidden behind anything.

blocks.title: What it isn't
blocks.body: It does not detect a fall. It does not predict one. It doesn't know where you are, doesn't read your messages, and tells nobody anything you didn't send yourself.

S02.footer: Education and self-management support. Not a diagnosis or treatment.

S03.title: Consent & privacy
S03.headline: What we hold, and what we don't.

blocks.title: Held on your phone
blocks.body: How steady you felt, your minutes, your notes, the wobbles you wrote down, and who you've picked to help. These stay here.

blocks.title: Shared with your care team
blocks.body: How steady you felt and how much you were on your feet, as a monthly summary, and only once you've read it. Never your notes, and never anything you told Dev.

blocks.title: You can leave
blocks.body: Export or delete all of it whenever you like. Deletion is finished rather than hidden, and Carol's view goes with it the same moment.

items.title: Share a monthly summary with my care team

S03.footer: You can change either choice later in Settings.

S04.title: First week
S04.headline: Carry on as you normally would.
S04.sub: Nothing to change this week. We're writing down what an ordinary week looks like, in your words, so that later on there's something honest to compare against.

blocks.title: What you've told us so far
blocks.body: Steadiest out on the flat. Least steady on the back step, and getting out of the low chair in the front room.
All of this is what you told us. Steady has no sensors, measures nothing, and does not treat any of it as a clinical reading.

blocks.title: You don't have to wait the week out
blocks.body: Five days is plenty to be going on with. Start now and we'll note that the picture is partial.

S05.title: What you're working towards
S05.headline: What would you like to be able to do?
S05.sub: Something you'd notice from the inside. Not a score, and not something a chart would tell you.

items.title: The shop and back without stopping
items.body: Wednesday, the long way round the green.

items.title: Out of the front room chair without using my hands
items.body: People usually give this one a good few weeks, and it comes back in small pieces.

items.title: Standing at the sink for the whole washing up
items.body: A quiet one. Also a good one.

blocks.title: How many days a week feels right?
blocks.body: Pick the number you'd manage in a bad week, not a good one.

blocks.title: When suits you?
blocks.body: Optional. A reminder is a reminder — nothing is recorded if you ignore it.

blocks.title: Nobody else sets this
blocks.body: Steady never picks your target, never raises it quietly behind you, and never moves it because a week went badly. Carol cannot change it, and neither can Dev without asking you first.

S06.title: Review your plan
S06.headline: Your plan is ready.
S06.sub: One last look. Any part of it can change now or later, and changing it doesn't need anyone's permission.

blocks.title: Four days a week, after breakfast
blocks.body: We'll only suggest going further when you tell us it's starting to feel easy. Not when a chart says so.

S08.title: Daily check-in
S08.headline: How's today been?
S08.sub: No right answers. A low number is as useful to us as a high one, and more useful to Dev.

blocks.title: How do you feel in yourself?
Did you get out this morning?
blocks.body: A no isn't a setback. Weather counts as a reason, and so does not fancying it.

blocks.title: Anything else today?
blocks.body: Optional. Tick anything that's true.

blocks.title: You ticked a wobble. Where was it?
blocks.body: Optional. It goes in your record and stays there — nobody is alerted, nothing is sent, and Carol won't see it unless you put it in Sunday's note yourself.

blocks.title: Dizzy standing up, more than once?
blocks.body: That's one to say out loud to a person rather than to an app, and it can have a plain cause worth sorting out. Dev is a coach, not a clinician, so anything like this goes to your care team the same day — and 988 answers at any hour if you're frightened tonight.
This is how you felt today, in your words. Steady doesn't measure it, can't tell you what it means, and never guesses what might happen next.

S08.footer: Private · Works offline · You can edit today's answers later

S09.title: Your next step
S09.headline: One thing, not five.
S09.sub: Based on a wobble on the back step, and a steady 8 everywhere else.

blocks.title: Write one line about what the back step was like.
blocks.body: Wet, dark, or just the height of it. Three of your wobbles have happened there, and Dev sees you Tuesday — that one sentence is worth more to him than a month of scores.

blocks.title: Or pick another
chips: Ask Carol about a second rail
Put the outside light on a timer
Mention it to Dev on Tuesday

blocks.body: Skipping is fine. We'll offer it again in a few days, and we won't ask why.

blocks.title: Why we don't hand you exercises
blocks.body: Steady doesn't set exercises, and it won't start. Dev works those out with you, and your doctor or a physical therapist is who says whether they're right for you at all. What this app does is remember what happened and put it in front of the two of you.

S10.title: Someone helping
S10.headline: This is everything Carol sees.
S10.sub: The whole list is on this screen. If something isn't on it, she can't see it — there's no second page and no small print.

blocks.title: Carol
blocks.body: Your daughter, twenty minutes away. Added on 4 March. She gets one note a week, on Sunday evening, and only after you've read it and pressed send.

items: How many mornings you got out this week
How steady you felt, as one number out of ten
Anything you type into the note yourself
Where you are. Steady has no location, on or off.
Your messages, your calls, or your contacts.
Anything live. There is no screen she can watch, and nothing reaches her between Sundays.
Your wobbles, unless you put one into the note yourself.
Your check-in answers, your notes, or anything Dev says to you.
Change your plan, answer a check-in, or switch anything on. There is no button for it on her side.

blocks.title: Sunday's note, as it stands
blocks.body: “Three mornings out. Felt steady, 8 out of 10. One wobble on the back step.” You'll see this exact wording on Sunday, and you can cut any line of it — or the whole thing — before it goes.

blocks.title: Stop sharing with Carol
blocks.body: Takes effect the moment you tap it, and you're not asked for a reason. Carol is told that sharing has stopped. She is not told why, and she cannot turn it back on.

blocks.title: The record is yours
blocks.body: Carol holds a copy of nothing. If you delete a week, it goes from her view in the same moment — she has a window, not a file.

S10.footer: A supporter helps. They don't decide, and they don't watch.

blocks.title: Why the dates are on the front
blocks.body: Anything that hasn't been checked in eighteen months comes down, rather than sitting here looking current.

blocks.title: What this library won't do
blocks.body: These explain. They don't prescribe. Nothing here sets you an exercise, changes a tablet, or tells you your risk of anything. None of it has seen your record.

blocks.title: If you want that conversation
blocks.body: It belongs with a qualified person. Dev replies within a day, and your doctor can go a good deal further than he can.

S11.footer: Reviewed before it goes up, and dated so you can see how old it is.

S12.title: Progress

blocks.unit: out of 10, how steady you felt

blocks.eyebrow: Last week was a quiet one, and it's still here
blocks.title: Two days out, not four.
blocks.body: Carol was ill and you stayed in. Nothing was reset, week 3 is still week 3, and those two flat days stay in the chart where they happened. An honest chart is worth more to you than a flattering one.

blocks.title: It's the back step, not the walk.
blocks.body: Both wobbles this month happened in the same place, and neither happened on the way to the shop. That's a fact about a step, and a step can be changed.

blocks.title: What this screen doesn't say
blocks.body: Nothing here predicts a fall. Steady can't do that, no phone can, and a number that pretended to would be worse than no number — it would either frighten you for nothing or reassure you wrongly.

blocks.title: Send this to your care team?
blocks.body: You'd read the exact file first: how steady you felt, minutes on your feet, and the wobbles you recorded. No notes. Nothing moves until you press send.

S12.footer: Nothing on this screen has been shared. It only leaves your phone if you ask it to.

S13.title: Support
S13.headline: A route to a person.
S13.sub: Nothing is sent until you've read it and pressed send.

blocks.title: In an emergency
blocks.body: If you've had a fall you can't get up from, or you're in danger, call 911 or your local emergency number now. Steady cannot call anyone for you, and it will never do it on its own.

blocks.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
blocks.body: Call or text 988 · English and Spanish · 24 hours

items: “Can you give me a ring when you get a minute?”

blocks.title: Services for older adults near you
blocks.body: There is a national line that puts people in touch with help in their own area — rails, transport, meals, someone to talk to. We haven't printed the number here because we couldn't confirm today that it's still the current one, and a wrong number in a bad hour is worse than no number. Your care team has it, and we'll put it on this screen once it's been checked.

blocks.title: Nothing here is automatic
blocks.body: No one on this screen is told anything unless you send it. This app cannot tell that something has happened to you, and it will never claim to.

S13.footer: Crisis numbers route to United States services.

blocks.body: Detail is off. A reminder on your lock screen says “Steady” and nothing else — not your check-in, not your plan, not why. Anyone who picks up your phone learns that an app reminded you. That's all.
